propositions.text: The claimant is a citizen of the Democratic Republic of the Congo claiming refugee protection under sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.
propositions.quote: The claimant, XXXX XXXX, is a citizen of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). He is claiming refugee protection under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (the Act).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is a DRC citizen claiming refugee protection under sections 96 and 97(1) of the Act, as stated by the court.

propositions.text: The claimant's allegations are summarized from his Basis of Claim Form.
propositions.quote: The allegations in support of this claim are found in the claimant's Basis of Claim Form (BOC Form) and can be summarized as follows:

paragraphs.summary: The court summarizes the claimant's allegations from his Basis of Claim Form.

propositions.text: The claimant fears arrest, torture, or death by authorities for reporting corrupt police officers and their wrongful acts.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges that he fears being arrested, tortured or killed by the authorities in his country for having reported corrupt police officers and their wrongful deeds XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in his country.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges fear of arrest, torture, or death for reporting corrupt police officers, as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: The claimant held various positions since 1966, including supervising monitoring activities.
propositions.quote: He held various positions with XXXX XXXX XXXX in his country. First, in 1966, he was the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and supervised XXXX who monitored XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant held various positions since 1966, including supervisory roles, as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: Between 19XX and 2006, the claimant held various positions including XXXX XXXX XXXX and from 2006 to 2014 was 'XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX'.
propositions.quote: Between 19XXXX and 19XXXX, he was responsible for XXXX XXXX. He held various positions in other cities, and from 19XXXX to 2006, he worked as XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX From 2006 to 2014 he was the [translation] "XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX."

paragraphs.summary: The claimant held various positions from 19XX to 2014, including 'XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX', as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: The claimant's recent duties included advising management and documenting problems, with both XXXX and administrative aspects.
propositions.quote: The claimant describes his duties in recent years as follows:1 [translation] 7. Despite my advancement in rank, I continued to perform the duties of XXXX advisor. My work had two aspects, a XXXX aspect and an administrative aspect. As part of these duties, I advised management about the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and, when there was a problem with XXXX XXXX XXXX, I was sent to document the problem. I also wrote reports about XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's recent duties involved advising management and documenting problems, as described by the claimant.

propositions.text: In 2003, the claimant discovered fictitious deserters on payroll and was shot in an assassination attempt.
propositions.quote: He alleges that, during the inspection of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in 2003, he discovered fictitious XXXX XXXX-deserters-listed on the payroll, and he issued a report on XXXXfictitious XXXX out of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. On XXXX XXXX, 2003, there was an attempt on his life in XXXX and he was shot in the XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges discovering payroll fraud in 2003 and surviving an assassination attempt, as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: In 20XX, the claimant acted as advisor gathering testimony on mass killings and was suspended with pay after reporting.
propositions.quote: In 20XXXX, during the crackdown on members of the Bundu-dia-Congo, he acted as XXXX advisor, gathering testimony from victims in order to submit a report to his superiors. During his investigation, it was determined that Rwandans XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX were responsible for mass killings. Following the report, he was suspended with pay from 20XXXX to 20XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant acted as advisor gathering testimony on mass killings and was suspended with pay after reporting, as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: In 2013, the claimant reported police summary executions of gangs to various organizations including the UN and Human Rights Watch.
propositions.quote: In XXXX 2013, when the authorities clamped down on the kulunas, gangs of delinquents, summary executions were carried out by the authorities, and two police officers involved told him about the wrongful deeds against the kulunas. The claimant reported those facts to the UDPS opposition party, to the national association of migrant and women's rights, to the UN, to Human Rights Watch and to the UN, which wrote a scathing report2 against the Congolese authorities.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant reported police summary executions of gangs to multiple organizations including the UN, as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: In 2014, police officers sought to arrest the claimant due to his reporting of police abuses.
propositions.quote: With regard to his leaving the DRC for Canada, the claimant wrote that on or about XXXX XXXX, 2014, a group of police officers under the orders of General Kanyama went looking for him at his home in the morning in order to arrest him as a result of his reporting police abuses against the groups of delinquents.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant states police sought to arrest him in 2014 due to his reporting of abuses, as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: The claimant fled and restricted movements in 2014 fearing General Kanyama and serious danger to his life.
propositions.quote: Since he feared General Kanyama, he fled his home and restricted his movements because he thought that his life was in serious danger in XXXX 2014.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant fled and restricted movements in 2014 fearing serious danger from General Kanyama, as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: A friend helped the claimant obtain an American visa in 2015 and find safe contacts to leave DRC without arrest.
propositions.quote: A friend helped him to obtain his American visa in XXXX 2015. He explained his delay in leaving the DRC after he obtained his American visa as follows: since he wanted to leave the country without being arrested by the authorities, his friend helped him to find good contacts so that he could get through the Kinshasa airport and leave his country.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant obtained an American visa in 2015 and delayed leaving DRC to avoid arrest, as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: The claimant left DRC in 2015 for Chicago and entered Canada at Fort Erie on April 26, 2015, claiming refugee protection that day.
propositions.quote: He left the DRC on XXXX XXXX, 2015, for Chicago, United States. He entered Canada at Fort Erie on April 26, 2015,3 and claimed refugee protection that same day.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant left DRC in 2015, entered Canada at Fort Erie on April 26, 2015, and claimed refugee protection that day, as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges he was XXXX XXXX XXXX since 19XX and his last position was 'XXXX XXXX XXXX'; a notice of exclusion under 1F(a) and (c) was sent to the Minister.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges in his Basis of Claim Form (BOC Form) that he had been XXXX XXXX XXXX in his country since 19XXXX and that his last position XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in his country was [translation] "XXXX XXXX XXXX." A notice of exclusion under 1F(a) and (c) was sent to the Minister in accordance with the requirements of rule 26.4

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges XXXX XXXX XXXX since 19XX and last position 'XXXX XXXX XXXX'; a notice of exclusion was sent to the Minister, as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: The Minister sent a notice of intervention asking the panel to reject the refugee claim for lack of credibility.
propositions.quote: On November 25, 2015, the Minister sent the panel a written notice of intervention.5 The Minister is asking the panel to reject the claimant's the refugee protection claim, submitting that his claim lacks credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister asks the panel to reject the refugee claim for lack of credibility, as stated by the Minister.

propositions.text: The Minister is not requesting exclusion of the claimant in the notice of intervention.
propositions.quote: In his notice of intervention, the Minister is not asking that the claimant be excluded.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister does not request exclusion of the claimant, as stated by the Minister.

propositions.text: The claimant arrived in Canada on May 26, 2015, with his Congolese passport and American visa; certified copies are on record.
propositions.quote: According to the evidence on record, the claimant arrived in Canada on May 26, 2015 (not on April 26, 2015), with his Congolese passport and the American visa he had obtained in XXXX 2015; certified copies of these are on record.6

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant arrived in Canada on May 26, 2015, with valid documents, correcting the claimant's date.

propositions.text: The claimant's identity was established after document verification in his presence.
propositions.quote: After verifying the said documents in his presence, his identity was established.

paragraphs.summary: The court found the claimant's identity established after document verification.

propositions.text: The claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under sections 96 or 97 of the Act.
propositions.quote: The claimant is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection" under sections 96 or 97 of the Act.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under the Act.

propositions.text: The key issue is the credibility of the claimant's story, which the panel did not believe for stated reasons.
propositions.quote: The determinative issue in this refugee protection claim is the credibility of the claimant's story, which the panel did not believe for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The court identifies the key issue as the claimant's credibility, which the panel did not believe.

propositions.text: The panel considered documents provided by claimant's counsel after the hearing.
propositions.quote: In its decision, the panel also considered the documents provided by the claimant's counsel after the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The panel considered documents provided by claimant's counsel after the hearing, the court states.

propositions.text: Claimant is 74 years old, moves and speaks slowly but understands questions well and expresses himself well.
propositions.quote: The claimant is a 74-year-old man whose physical movements are very slow. He speaks slowly but he expresses himself well, and he understood very well the questions put to him by the panel and his counsel at the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is 74, moves and speaks slowly but understands and expresses himself well, the court finds.

propositions.text: Claimant's answers were often evasive even to simple questions.
propositions.quote: Nevertheless, his answers were often evasive, even when they were very simple and clear.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's answers were often evasive even to simple questions, the court finds.

propositions.text: Claimant's narrative and testimony contain discrepancies, contradictions and major implausibilities undermining his credibility about fear and persecution.
propositions.quote: His narrative and testimony contain discrepancies, contradictions and major implausibilities that have undermined his credibility regarding his story of fear and persecution from the authorities in his country.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's story has discrepancies and contradictions undermining his credibility, the court finds.

propositions.text: If claimant was sought by authorities since 2014, they would not have promoted him in 2015 given his suspension from 20XXXX until departure.
propositions.quote: According to the panel, if the claimant was sought by the authorities in his country since XXXX 2014, they would not have promoted him in 2015, given his allegation that he had been suspended from 20XXXX until his departure from his country.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found claimant's promotion in 2015 inconsistent with being sought and suspended since 2014.

propositions.text: Claimant did not claim asylum in the US where he stayed from XXXX to May 2015 and gave no reasonable explanation.
propositions.quote: Moreover, he did not claim asylum in the United States, where he stayed from XXXX to May 2015, and he did not provide any reasonable explanation.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found claimant did not claim asylum in the US and gave no reasonable explanation, undermining credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant was promoted as XXXX XXXX XXXX by president and prime minister on XXXX XXXX, 2015.
propositions.quote: First, according to the evidence, the claimant was promoted8 as XXXX XXXX XXXX by the president and prime minister of his country on XXXX XXXX, 2015, yet he stated that he had been suspended by XXXX authorities since XXXX 20XXXX because he had written a report incriminating high-ranking XXXXofficials.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found claimant was promoted by president and prime minister in 2015 despite suspension claim.

propositions.text: Claimant wrote in narrative he was suspended from 20XXXX to present and confirmed in testimony.
propositions.quote: The claimant wrote in his narrative that he has been suspended from 20XXXX to present, which he confirmed in his testimony.

propositions.text: Panel asked claimant to explain how he could be promoted in 2015 despite suspension.
propositions.quote: The panel therefore asked him to explain how he could have been promoted by an order of the president and the prime minister of his country on XXXX XXXX, 2015.

paragraphs.summary: The panel noted claimant's suspension claim and asked how he was promoted in 2015 despite it.

propositions.text: Claimant gave three theories: suspension was verbal; he lodged appeal; he suspected trap by authorities.
propositions.quote: He told the panel that he had three theories to suggest: a) his suspension in 20XXXX was made only verbally; b) he had lodged an appeal in 20XXXX challenging his lack of promotion; c) he suspected it was a trap laid by the authorities in order to arrest him.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant gave three theories to explain suspension and promotion inconsistency, the panel recorded.

propositions.text: Claimant gave a fourth theory to Agency: authorities unaware of suspension in XXXX 20XXXX.
propositions.quote: When the claimant was questioned by the Agency on this same topic, he proposed a fourth theory-the fact that the authorities were not aware that he had been suspended in XXXX 20XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant gave a fourth theory to Agency that authorities were unaware of suspension, the panel noted.

propositions.text: Claimant said he signed in weekly or twice weekly to receive pay while suspended, so written signs existed in file.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that, while he was suspended, he had to go to sign in each week in order to receive his pay, because he was on stand-by. In his testimony, he stated that he went to sign in twice a week! Therefore, there were written signs in his file indicating that he had been suspended.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant said he signed in weekly or twice weekly to receive pay, so suspension was documented, the panel noted.

propositions.text: Panel cannot explain how high-ranking official could be suspended by verbal notice from 20XXXX to today.
propositions.quote: Even considering the particular context of a country like the DRC, the panel cannot explain how a high-ranking XXXX such as the claimant-XXXX advisor to the XXXX XXXX, no less-could have been suspended by his superiors with only a verbal notice to this effect from 20XXXX to today.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found it implausible that a high-ranking official was suspended by verbal notice for years.

propositions.text: Panel questions how president and prime minister granted promotion without recommendation of superiors.
propositions.quote: Moreover, how does one explain that the president and the prime minister of the country granted a promotion to a high-ranking XXXX XXXX without the recommendation of his superiors?

paragraphs.summary: The panel found it implausible that promotion was granted without superiors' recommendation.

propositions.text: Claimant's explanation for promotion despite being sought and leaving secretly is illogical and implausible, so no credibility granted.
propositions.quote: To justify his promotion in XXXX 2015, despite his allegation that he was sought by the police in his country since XXXX XXXX, 2014, and had to leave his country secretly on XXXX XXXX, 2015, without any trouble from those same authorities, the claimant's explanation is so illogical and implausible that the panel grants it no credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found claimant's explanation for promotion despite being sought and leaving secretly illogical and not credible.

propositions.text: Claimant has not established suspension and persecution by authorities or future risk due to activities in his country.
propositions.quote: The claimant has not established that he was suspended and persecuted by the authorities in his country because of his activities XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in his country, or that he would be in the future.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found claimant did not establish suspension, persecution, or future risk due to his activities.

propositions.text: UN report on kulunas from 2014 does not establish claimant faces risk because sources are anonymous.
propositions.quote: The panel read the UN report on the kulunas written by the UN in 2014. That report does not establish that the claimant faces a risk in his country because the sources are anonymous.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found the UN report does not establish risk to claimant because sources are anonymous.

propositions.text: International reports never identify sources; if claimant was source, authorities would not know this.
propositions.quote: Moreover, as his counsel indicated, the reports from international organizations, like the UN, never identify their sources. If the claimant was the source of the information in the October 2014 UN report, as his counsel states in his last exhibit, the authorities in his country would not know this.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found international reports do not identify sources, so authorities would not know if claimant was source.

propositions.text: Claimant did not provide evidence to corroborate incriminating report or explain suspension and promotion inconsistency.
propositions.quote: As for the supposed incriminating report written by the claimant in 20XXXX, he did not provide the panel with evidence to corroborate his testimony. He also failed to give a reasonable explanation as to why he was suspended yet promoted in 2015 by the authorities in his country.

propositions.text: If claimant wrote incriminating report, authorities have had it long, so it is no longer secret held by claimant.
propositions.quote: Moreover, if he did write an incriminating report that he submitted to his superiors, then the authorities in his country have been in possession of that report for a long time, so it is no longer a secret held by the claimant.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found claimant did not corroborate incriminating report or explain suspension and promotion; report is no longer secret.

propositions.text: Claimant said he left country secretly in XXXX 2015 and lived in hiding fearing authorities since 2014.
propositions.quote: According to the claimant, he had to leave his country secretly in XXXX 2015, and he was living in hiding because he had feared the authorities in his country since XXXX 2014.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant said he left secretly in 2015 and lived in hiding fearing authorities since 2014, the panel recorded.

propositions.text: Claimant said he restricted movements since 2014 fearing arrest or death by General Kanyama, whose abuses he denounced.
propositions.quote: Moreover, he stated that he had been living in hiding and restricted his movements since XXXX 2014 because he was afraid of being arrested or killed by General Kanyama, whose abuses he had denounced.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant said he restricted movements since 2014 fearing arrest or death by General Kanyama, the panel recorded.

propositions.text: The claimant left his country in 2015 using his own passport and had police authorization to go to the US.
propositions.quote: the claimant left his country in XXXX 2015 using his own passport and, according to his own testimony, he was issued an authorization for departure by the police authorities in his country in order to go to the United States in XXXX 2015.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant left his country in 2015 with his own passport and police authorization to go to the US, according to his testimony.

propositions.text: The claimant said a friend helped him get authorization to leave and obtain an American visa.
propositions.quote: he answered that his friend had helped him get the authorization to leave his country and obtain the American visa.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said a friend helped him get authorization to leave and obtain an American visa.

propositions.text: In his BOC Form, the claimant said his friend helped him leave the airport, not obtain the visa.
propositions.quote: he states that his friend had helped him with leaving the Kinshasa airport, as he did not want to be arrested by the authorities, not with obtaining an American visa, as he stated in his testimony.

paragraphs.summary: In his BOC Form, the claimant said his friend helped him leave the airport, not obtain the visa, unlike his testimony.

propositions.text: It is not credible that a high-ranking person sought by police could leave with his own documents, despite corruption.
propositions.quote: The panel does not find it credible that a high-ranking XXXX XXXX in the DRC who was sought by the police in his country could have left with his own identity documents, even if the panel considers the widespread corruption in that country.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds it not credible that a high-ranking person sought by police could leave with his own documents despite corruption.

propositions.text: The claimant said authorities knew he was traveling abroad for medical treatment, so departure was not secret.
propositions.quote: in his testimony, the claimant clearly stated that the authorities were aware that he was travelling abroad to receive medical treatment. So, this was not a secret departure from the country, contrary to what the claimant stated.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said authorities knew he was traveling abroad for medical treatment, so departure was not secret.

propositions.text: The claimant fears persecution due to ethnicity and political membership in opposition party UDPS.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges that he also fears persecution by reason of his ethnicity and his political membership in the opposition party, the UDPS.

propositions.text: The claimant's answers about this fear were vague and evasive, even to simple questions.
propositions.quote: His answers were vague and evasive, even when the questions were simple.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges fear of persecution due to ethnicity and political membership, but his answers were vague and evasive.

propositions.text: The claimant hesitated and gave inconsistent answers about his UDPS membership.
propositions.quote: He hesitated for a long time; he first answered that he was a supporter, then stated that he had been a member since the party was founded in 1982; then, in answer to his counsel's question, he replied that XXXX XXXX were not authorized to be members of political parties in the DRC.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant hesitated and gave inconsistent answers about his UDPS membership.

propositions.text: The claimant said he did not get evidence from UDPS about his reports because he had to leave secretly and quickly.
propositions.quote: he alleged that he had to leave the country secretly and quickly.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said he did not get evidence from UDPS because he had to leave secretly and quickly.

propositions.text: The panel did not believe the claimant left secretly or was persecuted due to reports incriminating police.
propositions.quote: The panel did not believe that the claimant left his country in XXXX 2015 without the knowledge of the authorities there. Without any evidence to corroborate the alleged persecution due to reports incriminating the XXXX XXXX, the panel did not believe the claimant.

paragraphs.summary: The panel did not believe the claimant left secretly or was persecuted due to reports incriminating police.

propositions.text: Evidence shows claimant was a high-ranking member of state apparatus, promoted in 2015 by president and prime minister.
propositions.quote: the claimant had been a high-ranking member of XXXX XXXX XXXX in his country since 19XXXX. He worked with XXXX XXXX in various cities, including XXXX from 19XXXX to present. He was promoted to XXXX XXXX XXXX on XXXX XXXX, 2015, by the president and prime minister of the DRC.

propositions.text: The claimant was more part of the state apparatus than an opponent to it.
propositions.quote: The claimant was more a part of the country's state apparatus than an opponent to that apparatus.

paragraphs.summary: Evidence shows claimant was a high-ranking state member promoted in 2015; he was part of the state apparatus, not an opponent.

propositions.text: In Schedule A form, claimant did not indicate UDPS membership but did indicate Red Cross.
propositions.quote: at question 9 in his Schedule A form, he gives no indication that he was a member of the UDPS, but he did indicate the Red Cross.

propositions.text: Evidence does not establish claimant was a political opponent in DRC.
propositions.quote: The evidence does not establish that the claimant was a political opponent in the DRC.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant did not indicate UDPS membership in Schedule A; evidence does not establish he was a political opponent.

propositions.text: Claimant fears persecution due to ethnicity as a Luba tribe member linked to opposition.
propositions.quote: The claimant further stated for the first time at the hearing that he fears persecution by reason of his ethnicity. He is a member of the Luba tribe, which is often associated with opponents of the current Kabila regime.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant alleges fear of persecution due to ethnicity as Luba tribe member linked to opposition.

propositions.text: Claimant was a high-ranking official; evidence does not support persecution due to ethnicity.
propositions.quote: According to the evidence, the claimant was a high-ranking XXXX XXXX in his country by his own acknowledgement. The evidence does not allow for a conclusion that the claimant was or would be persecuted by reason of his ethnicity.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant was a high-ranking official; evidence does not support persecution due to ethnicity.

propositions.text: Claimant fears returning as a XXXX XXXX but authorities knew he went abroad for medical treatment.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he fears returning to his country because he is a XXXX XXXX According to the evidence, the claimant stated that the authorities are aware that he went abroad for medical treatment.

propositions.text: Claimant has not shown he could not prove this if he returned to DRC.
propositions.quote: Consequently, he has not established that he could not prove this if he returned to the DRC.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant fears returning as XXXX XXXX but authorities knew he went abroad; he has not shown he could not prove this if returned.

propositions.text: Claimant got US visa and left country in 2015, though he said he hid since 2014 and decided then to leave.
propositions.quote: the claimant obtained his American visa on XXXX XXXX, 2015, and that he left his country on XXXX XXXX, 2015, although he stated that he had been in hiding since XXXX 2014 and had decided at that time to leave the DRC.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant got US visa and left country in 2015, though he said he hid since 2014 and decided then to leave.

propositions.text: Claimant said he did not leave earlier to avoid police capture.
propositions.quote: He answered that he was avoiding being captured by the police.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant said he did not leave earlier to avoid police capture.

propositions.text: Panel did not believe claimant was sought by authorities; if so, he would have used visa earlier.
propositions.quote: As noted by the panel earlier, it did not believe that the claimant was sought by the authorities in his country. If that had been the case, he would have used the visa he obtained in XXXX to leave the DRC.

propositions.text: This undermines claimant's credibility.
propositions.quote: This further undermines his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: Panel did not believe claimant was sought by authorities; if so, he would have used visa earlier, undermining credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant stayed in US months without claiming asylum; said friends advised him to come to Canada.
propositions.quote: he stayed in the United States from XXXX XXXX to May 26 without claiming asylum. When asked to explain why, he answered that his friends had advised him to come to Canada; he was not interested in claiming asylum in the United States, and that DRC authorities often travel to the United States.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant stayed in US months without claiming asylum; said friends advised him to come to Canada.

propositions.text: Claimant's daughter lives in Canada, which could explain claim, but claimant did not mention this.
propositions.quote: The panel notes that the claimant's daughter lives in Canada, which could have explained his decision to claim refugee protection in Canada, but he did not mention this to the panel.

propositions.text: Other explanations claimant gave are not reasonable; he stayed months in US before claiming in Canada.
propositions.quote: The other three explanations given by the claimant are not reasonable. He stayed in the United States for XXXX months before coming to file his claim here.

propositions.text: If claimant feared persecution, he would have claimed asylum in the US.
propositions.quote: If the claimant feared persecution in the DRC and had left his country because of that, he would have claimed asylum in the United States.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's daughter lives in Canada but he did not mention this; other explanations are unreasonable; he would have claimed asylum in US if fearing persecution.

propositions.text: Lack of US asylum claim and no reasonable explanation undermine claimant's credibility.
propositions.quote: The lack of a claim in the United States and the lack of a reasonable explanation for not filing a claim for asylum in a country that is a signatory to the Convention, just as Canada is, adds to the other factors that undermine the claimant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: Lack of US asylum claim and no reasonable explanation undermine claimant's credibility.

propositions.text: The claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under sections 96 or 97 of the Act.
propositions.quote: The claimant is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection" under sections 96 or 97 of the Act

propositions.text: The claimant did not establish a serious possibility of persecution on a Convention ground.
propositions.quote: he did not establish that there is a serious possibility of persecution on a Convention ground

propositions.text: The claimant did not establish any risk under subsection 97(1) if returned to the DRC.
propositions.quote: nor any risk under to subsection 97(1) if he were to return to the DRC

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection, lacking serious persecution or risk if returned to DRC.

propositions.text: The refugee protection claim is rejected.
propositions.quote: The refugee protection claim is rejected

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the refugee protection claim.
